library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2024_docetaxel"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2024_docetaxel"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-024-09913-y>
* Open-access full text and Supplementary file 1: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11254990/>

Wang 2024 fitted one population PK model to total and unbound plasma docetaxel
measured in the same nine men twice: once after their standard 1-h intravenous
(IV) docetaxel infusion, and once after a single oral docetaxel dose taken 1 h
after 15 mg of the intestinal P-glycoprotein inhibitor encequidar ("oDox + E").
The model was then used to ask whether any practical oDox + E regimen could
match the unbound exposure of IV docetaxel (a GO / NO-GO decision).

The final model (Supplementary file 1, "Final Model (Combined)" column, and the
structure diagram in Supplement 2) is a three-compartment model written for
**unbound** docetaxel. The central state therefore holds the unbound-equivalent
amount, `Cunbound = central / vc`, and total docetaxel is reconstructed through a
constant binding constant `B = 1 / fu`. The fraction unbound differs between the
two formulations (0.67% for the polysorbate-80 IV product, 1.02% after oDox + E),
so the packaged model takes the route as the covariate `ROUTE_IV`. As the paper
notes, total clearance is `CL * fu_iv = 8570 * 0.0067 = 57.3 L/h`.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Wang_2024_docetaxel")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta
TV <- list(
  cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]), vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]),
  q = exp(th[["lq"]]), vp = exp(th[["lvp"]]),
  q2 = exp(th[["lq2"]]), vp2 = exp(th[["lvp2"]]),
  ka = exp(th[["lka"]]), tlag = exp(th[["ltlag"]]),
  fdepot = plogis(th[["logitfdepot"]]),
  fu_iv = exp(th[["lfu_iv"]]), fu_po = exp(th[["lfu_po"]])
)
str(TV)
```

# Population

Nine patients with metastatic prostate cancer who were receiving IV docetaxel
completed the phase I open-label, two-period, two-treatment study (Wang 2024
Methods, "Study design"; trial reported by Jackson et al., reference 21 of the
paper). The first period was the standard of care, about 75 mg/m^2 IV docetaxel
over 1 h; the second, at least 3 weeks later, was a single oDox + E dose at
75, 150 or 300 mg/m^2. Total docetaxel was measured in every sample (24 after
IV, 23 after oDox + E; LLOQ 2 ng/mL) and unbound docetaxel in 7 and 8
optimal-design-selected samples per patient (LLOQ 0.084 ng/mL; 25% below LLOQ,
handled with the M6 method). The paper reports no age, weight or body surface
area summary, and covariates were not tested because of the small sample.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Wang_2024_docetaxel")()$population`.

# Source trace

All values come from the "Final Model (Combined)" column of Wang 2024
Supplementary file 1 (sub-model 6).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (unbound CL) | log(8570 L/h) | Supplement 1, CL(/F) |
| `lvc` | log(3500 L) | Supplement 1, Vc |
| `lq` | log(1250 L/h) | Supplement 1, Qp1 |
| `lvp` | log(9450 L) | Supplement 1, Vp1 |
| `lq2` | log(2810 L/h) | Supplement 1, Qp2 |
| `lvp2` | log(61900 L) | Supplement 1, Vp2 |
| `lka` | log(0.223 1/h) | Supplement 1, ka |
| `ltlag` | log(0.242 h) | Supplement 1, ALAG |
| `logitfdepot` | logit(0.25) | Supplement 1, F = 25% |
| `lfu_iv` | log(0.0067) | Supplement 1, f unbound IV = 0.67% |
| `lfu_po` | log(0.0102) | Supplement 1, f unbound PO = 1.02% |
| `etalcl`, `etalka`, `etaltlag`, `etalvc`, `etalvp` | 0.27^2, 0.47^2, 0.03^2, 0.63^2, 1.48^2 | Supplement 1, BSV CL 27%, ka 47%, ALAG 3%, Vc 63%, Vp1 148% |
| `etalogitfdepot` | 0.71^2 | Supplement 1, BSV logitF = 0.71 (logit-scale SD) |
| `etalfu_iv`, `etalfu_po` | 0.28^2, 0.72^2 | Supplement 1, BSV BIV 28%, BPO 72% |
| `addSdIv`, `propSdIv` | 0.001 ng/mL, 0.143 | Supplement 1, Tot IV add '<0.001', Tot IV prop |
| `addSdOral`, `propSdOral` | 0.199 ng/mL, 0.322 | Supplement 1, Tot PO add, Tot PO prop |
| `addSdIv_Cunbound`, `propSdIv_Cunbound` | 0.005 ng/mL, 0.538 | Supplement 1, UF IV add, UF IV prop |
| `addSdOral_Cunbound`, `propSdOral_Cunbound` | 0.003 ng/mL, 0.337 | Supplement 1, UF PO add, UF PO prop |
| Three-compartment linear disposition of unbound drug, oral input with F, ka and lag | n/a | Results "Final model"; Supplement 2 |
| `Cc = Cunbound / fu`, `fu` by route | n/a | Supplement 1 abbreviations (fu = 1 / B); Supplement 2 |

# Closed-form checks

The paper's own derived quantity is total IV clearance, 57.3 L/h. A typical
patient's unbound AUC after a dose is `F * Dose / CL`, and total AUC is that
divided by `fu`.

```{r closed-form}
cl_total_iv <- TV$cl * TV$fu_iv
cl_total_iv
stopifnot(abs(cl_total_iv - 57.3) / 57.3 < 0.01)

# Total steady-state volume implied by the tabulated parameters.
vss_total_iv <- (TV$vc + TV$vp + TV$vp2) * TV$fu_iv
vss_total_iv
```

The tabulated parameters give a total-docetaxel Vss of
`r round(vss_total_iv)` L, against the 425 L quoted in the paper's Discussion;
the difference is discussed under Assumptions and deviations.

# Virtual cohort

The trial doses were 75 mg/m^2 IV and 75, 150 or 300 mg/m^2 oDox + E. The
paper's own simulations convert 75 mg/m^2 to 130 mg using a body surface area
of 1.7 m^2 (Table 2), and the same conversion is used here for every arm. Each
virtual patient receives a single dose of one regimen.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240314)
n_per_arm <- 50L
bsa <- 1.7
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,               ~route_iv, ~dose_mgm2,
  "IV 75 mg/m^2",           1L,        75,
  "oDox+E 75 mg/m^2",       0L,        75,
  "oDox+E 150 mg/m^2",      0L,        150,
  "oDox+E 300 mg/m^2",      0L,        300
) |>
  mutate(amt = round(dose_mgm2 * bsa), arm = row_number())

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 168, by = 1))))

make_arm <- function(a) {
  ids <- (a$arm - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = a$amt, evid = 1L,
    rate = if (a$route_iv == 1L) a$amt else 0,
    cmt = if (a$route_iv == 1L) "central" else "depot",
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, rate = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = a$treatment, ROUTE_IV = a$route_iv)
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(split(arms, arms$arm), make_arm)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240314)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment"), returnType = "data.frame")
sim_pk <- sim |> filter(!is.na(Cc))
```

# Replicate published figures

Figure 1 of Wang 2024 shows the observed total and unbound profiles of the nine
patients; Figure 6 overlays the individual fits. The simulated 5th, 50th and
95th percentiles below should bracket those observations: IV total docetaxel
peaks at roughly 1000-2000 ng/mL and unbound at about 5-15 ng/mL, while oDox + E
total docetaxel peaks at roughly 50-200 ng/mL and unbound at about 0.3-2 ng/mL.

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 7}
sim_pk |>
  filter(time <= 72) |>
  select(treatment, time, Cc, Cunbound) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cunbound), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "Cc", "Total", "Unbound")) |>
  group_by(treatment, analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(conc, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(Q50 > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 1e-3), ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(analyte = c("Total", "Unbound"), lloq = c(2, 0.084)),
    aes(yintercept = lloq), linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Docetaxel (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated total and unbound docetaxel (median, 90% interval)",
    caption = "Compare with Figures 1 and 6 of Wang 2024. Dashed: LLOQ (2 and 0.084 ng/mL)."
  )
```

```{r figure-1-check}
peaks <- sim_pk |>
  group_by(treatment, id) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), cmax_u = max(Cunbound), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(median_cmax = median(cmax), median_cmax_unbound = median(cmax_u), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(peaks, digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated peak total and unbound docetaxel (ng/mL).")

iv_peak <- peaks |> filter(treatment == "IV 75 mg/m^2")
# Figure 1A/B: observed IV peaks of ~1000-2000 ng/mL total and ~5-15 ng/mL unbound.
stopifnot(
  iv_peak$median_cmax > 700, iv_peak$median_cmax < 3000,
  iv_peak$median_cmax_unbound > 4, iv_peak$median_cmax_unbound < 20
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Wang 2024 reports no NCA table, so PKNCA is used here for two purposes: to
summarise the simulated exposure by arm for total and unbound docetaxel, and to
check the solver against each subject's closed-form unbound AUC0-inf,
`F_i * Dose / CL_i` (F = 1 for IV), using that subject's own drawn parameters.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sim_pk |>
  select(id, time, treatment, Cc, Cunbound)
nca_input <- bind_rows(
  nca_input,
  nca_input |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0, Cunbound = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(
    route = ifelse(ROUTE_IV == 1, "intravascular", "extravascular"),
    duration = ifelse(ROUTE_IV == 1, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment, route, duration)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)

run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc_df <- nca_input |>
    rename(conc = all_of(conc_col)) |>
    select(id, time, treatment, conc)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | treatment + id,
                               concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                               route = "route", duration = "duration", doseu = "mg")
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

nca_total <- run_nca("Cc")
nca_unbound <- run_nca("Cunbound")

summary(nca_total)
summary(nca_unbound)
```

```{r pknca-closed-form}
indiv <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), fdepot = first(fdepot), .groups = "drop")
auc_check <- as.data.frame(nca_unbound) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  select(id, treatment, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(dose_df |> select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  left_join(indiv, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    f = ifelse(grepl("^IV", treatment), 1, fdepot),
    auc_closed = f * amt / cl * 1000,
    pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf - auc_closed) / auc_closed
  )

auc_check |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff),
    q90_abs_pct_diff = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA unbound AUC0-inf versus each subject's closed-form F * Dose / CL (percent difference).")

# Both sides use the same drawn parameters; the only differences are the
# trapezoidal AUC and the log-linear extrapolation past 168 h of a profile
# whose terminal half-life is about 21 h for a typical patient but can be
# much longer for a subject with a large Vp1.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_check$pct_diff)) < 3,
  quantile(abs(auc_check$pct_diff), 0.9) < 10
)
```

# GO / NO-GO probability of target attainment (Figures 7-9)

Wang 2024 compared each oDox + E regimen with 130 mg IV docetaxel over 1 h in
the same virtual patient. For each effective concentration (EC) of unbound
docetaxel from 0.1 to 1 ng/mL, the AUC of the unbound profile above the EC
(AUCOEC, Figure 2) was computed over 24 h on a 3-minute grid (Table 2). An
oDox + E regimen succeeded for a patient when its AUCOEC was at least 80% of
that patient's IV AUCOEC (a 20% non-inferiority margin, Equation 1); the
probability of target attainment (PTA) is the share of successes (Equation 2).
Two- and three-dose regimens were evaluated by multiplying the single-dose
AUCOEC by the number of doses (complete washout between daily doses was
assumed). Unbound docetaxel does not depend on `fu`, so only the disposition,
absorption and bioavailability parameters matter here; the paper simulated
without residual error.

The paired design needs every regimen to share one patient's random effects.
The effects are therefore drawn in base R from the model's omega matrix and
passed to the typical-value model, so each virtual patient is solved once per
regimen with identical parameters. The paper used 1000 virtual patients; 200
are used here.

```{r pta-simulate}
set.seed(20240315)
n_pt <- 200L
omega <- ui$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_pt * nrow(omega)), n_pt) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,  ~route_iv, ~amt,
  "IV 130",  1L,        130,
  "PO 400",  0L,        400,
  "PO 450",  0L,        450,
  "PO 500",  0L,        500,
  "PO 550",  0L,        550,
  "PO 600",  0L,        600
) |>
  mutate(k = row_number())

grid24 <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)
pta_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(r) {
  g <- regimens[r, ]
  ids <- (g$k - 1L) * n_pt + seq_len(n_pt)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = g$amt, evid = 1L,
           rate = if (g$route_iv == 1L) g$amt else 0,
           cmt = if (g$route_iv == 1L) "central" else "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = grid24) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, rate = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(regimen = g$regimen, patient = id - (g$k - 1L) * n_pt, ROUTE_IV = g$route_iv)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

pta_params <- pta_events |>
  distinct(id, patient) |>
  bind_cols(as.data.frame(eta[pta_events |> distinct(id, patient) |> pull(patient), , drop = FALSE])) |>
  select(-patient)

pta_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = pta_events, params = pta_params,
  keep = c("regimen", "patient"), returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cunbound))
```

```{r pta-compute}
ec_levels <- seq(0.1, 1.0, by = 0.1)
trap_above <- function(time, conc, ec) {
  y <- pmax(conc - ec, 0)
  sum(diff(time) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
}
aucoec <- pta_sim |>
  group_by(regimen, patient) |>
  reframe(ec = ec_levels, aucoec = vapply(ec_levels, function(e) trap_above(time, Cunbound, e), numeric(1)))

target <- aucoec |>
  filter(regimen == "IV 130") |>
  transmute(patient, ec, target = 0.8 * aucoec)

pta <- aucoec |>
  filter(regimen != "IV 130") |>
  inner_join(target, by = c("patient", "ec")) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(n_doses = 1:3) |>
  group_by(regimen, n_doses, ec) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(n_doses * aucoec >= target), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(dose_mg = as.numeric(sub("PO ", "", regimen)))
```

```{r figures-7-9, fig.height = 7}
pta |>
  mutate(
    doses = factor(n_doses, labels = c("Single dose (Figure 7)", "Two doses (Figure 8)", "Three doses (Figure 9)")),
    dose_mg = factor(dose_mg)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(ec, pta, colour = dose_mg)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80) +
  facet_wrap(~doses, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = ec_levels) +
  labs(
    x = "Effective concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Probability of target attainment (%)",
    colour = "oDox + E dose (mg)",
    caption = "Replicates Figures 7, 8 and 9 of Wang 2024 (target: 130 mg IV docetaxel over 1 h)."
  )
```

The maintainers digitised selected points from Figures 7-9 (read to about
+/- 2 percentage points); the three-dose 600 mg value at 1 ng/mL (56%) is also
printed in the Results, and the Discussion gives 74% for the single 600 mg dose.

```{r pta-compare}
published_pta <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n_doses, ~dose_mg, ~ec, ~pta_published,
  1L, 600, 0.1, 72.5,
  1L, 600, 0.3, 46,
  1L, 600, 0.5, 22.5,
  1L, 400, 0.1, 11,
  2L, 600, 0.1, 97.5,
  2L, 600, 0.3, 91,
  2L, 600, 0.5, 78.5,
  2L, 600, 0.7, 60,
  2L, 600, 1.0, 33.5,
  2L, 400, 0.1, 84.5,
  2L, 400, 0.3, 52.5,
  2L, 400, 0.5, 21.5,
  3L, 600, 0.3, 97,
  3L, 600, 0.5, 91,
  3L, 600, 0.7, 80,
  3L, 600, 1.0, 56,
  3L, 400, 0.1, 96.5,
  3L, 400, 0.3, 80.5,
  3L, 400, 0.5, 52,
  3L, 400, 1.0, 7
)

pta_cmp <- published_pta |>
  left_join(pta |> mutate(ec = round(ec, 1)), by = c("n_doses", "dose_mg", "ec")) |>
  mutate(difference = pta - pta_published)

pta_cmp |>
  select(n_doses, dose_mg, ec, pta_published, pta, difference) |>
  rename(
    "Doses" = n_doses, "oDox + E dose (mg)" = dose_mg, "EC (ng/mL)" = ec,
    "Published PTA (%)" = pta_published, "Simulated PTA (%)" = pta,
    "Difference (points)" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated vs. published (digitised) PTA.")

# Gate only on the two values the paper prints in its text: 74% for a single
# 600 mg dose (Discussion; 72.5% at 0.1 ng/mL in Figure 7) and 56% for three
# 600 mg doses at 1 ng/mL (Results). The cohort is drawn with base R only, so
# it is the same on every machine; its Monte Carlo error at 200 patients is
# up to 3.5 points. A mis-read bioavailability or clearance moves either
# value by 15 points or more.
anchor_single <- pta_cmp |> filter(n_doses == 1L, dose_mg == 600, ec == 0.1)
anchor_triple <- pta_cmp |> filter(n_doses == 3L, dose_mg == 600, ec == 1.0)
stopifnot(
  abs(anchor_single$pta - 74) < 10,
  abs(anchor_triple$pta - 56) < 10
)
```

The two values printed in the text are reproduced, and so is the shape of the
GO / NO-GO result: no single dose reaches 80% at any EC, while two or three
daily 600 mg doses do at low EC. Away from those anchors the simulated curves
are flatter across dose than the published ones: the 400 mg regimens attain
the target more often at low EC and less often at high EC than in Figures 7-9,
and the 600 mg multiple-dose regimens less often at intermediate EC (by up to
about 20 points). The spread across dose at a fixed EC is driven almost
entirely by the between-patient variability of the bioavailability, and
simulating with the logit-scale SD of 0.71 tabulated in Supplement 1 gives a
wider spread than the published curves imply, while removing that variability
altogether gives a much narrower one. The paper's simulation code is not
published, so this is recorded as a known deviation rather than resolved by
changing a tabulated value.

```{r go-nogo}
pta |>
  group_by(n_doses) |>
  summarise(max_pta = max(pta), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Highest simulated PTA (%) over all doses and EC levels, by number of doses.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Unbound parameterisation.** Supplement 1 states that the parameters are "in
  the context of unbound docetaxel" and the Results give total clearance as
  `CL * fu_iv`; the central state therefore holds unbound-equivalent docetaxel
  and total concentration is `Cunbound / fu`.
- **Binding-constant variability.** The paper places exponential
  between-subject variability on the binding constants `B_IV` and `B_PO`
  (`B = 1 / fu`). The model carries it on `fu` instead; `exp(eta)` on `B` is
  `exp(-eta)` on `fu`, which is the same log-normal distribution.
- **Omega scale.** The Supplement 1 footnote says the BSV values are CVs
  "calculated as the square root of the omega value", so each variance is the
  square of the tabulated CV. The logit-F entry (0.71, no percent sign) is read
  as the SD on the logit scale. With it the single 600 mg dose comes close to
  the 74% PTA quoted in the Discussion (in closed form, at an effective
  concentration of zero, it gives exactly 74%).
- **PTA curves.** The simulated Figures 7-9 match the two PTA values printed
  in the text but are flatter across dose than the published curves (see the
  comparison table above); the paper's simulation code is not available to
  explain the difference, and no tabulated value was changed.
- **Vp2 variability.** BSV on Vp2 was estimated at 0% (RSE NA) and is omitted.
- **Residual error.** The additive SD for total docetaxel after IV is
  tabulated as "<0.001" ng/mL; the bound 0.001 ng/mL is used (negligible next
  to the 14.3% proportional term at these concentrations). The combined error
  is encoded as nlmixr2's standard additive-plus-proportional model; the
  paper does not state how the two terms were combined in NONMEM.
- **Correlated residuals (L2).** The final model let the residuals of the total
  and unbound measurements from the same blood sample be correlated (NONMEM
  L2 data item) but the correlation is not reported. The two outputs carry
  independent residual errors.
- **Total Vss.** The Discussion quotes a total-docetaxel Vss of 425 L; the
  tabulated volumes multiplied by `fu_iv` give about 502 L. The tabulated
  parameters are used unchanged, and they reproduce the paper's 57.3 L/h total
  clearance exactly.
- **Body surface area.** The paper reports no demographics; doses in mg/m^2
  are converted with the 1.7 m^2 used in the paper's own simulations.
- **Oral docetaxel alone.** The dashed "oral docetaxel alone (F = 8%)" curves
  of Figures 7-9 are not reproduced, because the paper does not say whether
  the bioavailability variability was kept when F was changed.
- **Correction.** A correction notice (doi:10.1007/s10928-024-09924-9) amends
  author affiliations only; no model value is affected.
